segments.content:
Chapter 162, Section 0159: How Many People Have Changed Because of You? The 2005 Gaokao had ended, and the first and second-year high school students were back in class, waiting for the impending final exams.

County No. 2 High School, First-Year Class 1 (Advanced Class).

The students had shifted all their desks forward, creating more space at the back of the classroom where two rows of stools were to be placed.

Why the stools?

To learn from Master Teacher Li Runze's advanced teaching methods, of course.

The leaders and fellow teachers hadn't arrived yet, but Li Runze had already walked into the classroom, full of vigor.

"I have some good news for everyone," Li Runze said, his face wreathed in smiles. "Your senior, your..."

"Chen Guiliang!"

"Hahahaha!"

Before he could finish, the students shouted "Chen Guiliang," and the whole class erupted in laughter.

Ever since their first high school Chinese class, these students in the advanced first-year class had heard Li Runze mention Chen Guiliang countless times.

After the laughter subsided, Li Runze continued, "I've told you all before, Chen Guiliang started two companies right after getting into Peking University. One of them is called ByteDance... See, when you're good at Chinese, even the names you pick for your companies are different. A 'byte' is a unit of measurement for computers, a cold computer term. Add 'dance,' and it immediately becomes romantic..."

At that very moment, leaders from the Education Bureau, school administrators, and Chinese teachers from other schools were filing into the back of the classroom and taking their seats.

The class bell hadn't rung yet, so they could listen to Li Runze brag for a while.

Li Runze said, "Among the internet companies in China right now, only Baidu's name can compare with ByteDance. 'Having searched for him hundreds and thousands of times in the crowd, suddenly I turn back, and there he is, in the dimmest candlelight.' Using Baidu as the name for a search engine is very fitting, and it has a poetic quality."

With that, he unscrewed the lid of his thermos and took a sip of goji berry tea.

Then he announced, "Chen Guiliang's company, ByteDance, has received 5 million USD in venture capital funding, with a post-money valuation of 30 million USD. Based on Chen Guiliang's shareholding percentage, your senior... is now worth 160 million!"

"Wow!"

The students gasped in amazement, then broke into a flurry of excited chatter.

The leaders and teachers sitting in the back, though they had already heard the news, couldn't help but feel a fresh sense of wonder.

This small city didn't produce many famous people.

Not counting figures from the past.

In recent years, there was the "Diving Queen" Gao Min, a few years ago Guo Xiaosi emerged, and now Rao Xueman was also quite popular.

Tan Weiwei wouldn't become famous until next year.

Chen Guiliang had truly become a leading figure, and his rise was astonishingly fast. At the beginning of the year, people were talking about his high book sales; now, he had directly become a hundred-millionaire.

The teachers who had come to observe the class were especially thinking to themselves: If Chen Guiliang were my student, I could brag about him for the rest of my life!

Li Runze, who had already been bragging for nearly a year, ignored the class bell that had just rung and continued to chat idly.

A model open class?

Leaders and colleagues here to observe?

To hell with it, I'll finish my bragging first.

Li Runze said to the students, "Behind every successful person is hard work and sweat. Don't just see your senior making big money and start fantasizing about your own future. Different stages of life have different goals. Let's take your Senior Chen as an example..."

Here we go again!

The students of First-Year Class 1 felt like their ears were about to grow calluses.

First-Year Class 6.

The politics teacher, Gao Zhan, wasn't teaching either. Instead, he sat on the teacher's platform with a cigarette dangling from his lips, puffing away and shooting the breeze with the students.

"Don't think politics is useless. This subject can cultivate your critical thinking and problem-solving skills, and it even includes economic principles. Why was Chen Guiliang able to build such a big company? It's because he laid a solid foundation in high school politics..."

Just then, a student raised his hand, "Teacher!"

"Speak," Gao Zhan said, annoyed at having his flow interrupted.

The student challenged him, "Why do you often quote *The Ugly Chinaman* and say that Bo Yang saw through to the inferior nature of the Chinese people? But on that TV show, Chen Guiliang said *The Ugly Chinaman* is a pile of shit?"

Gao Zhan opened his mouth but was left speechless, his face turning sour.

"Hahaha!"

Many students started laughing.

Gao Zhan tried to save face, "Chen Guiliang didn't truly understand *The Ugly Chinaman*."

The student pressed on, "Chen Guiliang recommended that Bo Yang read *A History of Chinese Thought*, saying that reading more would be good for him. Teacher, have you read that book?"

"I have, but I haven't finished it," Gao Zhan stubbed out his cigarette and picked up a practice worksheet. "Now, let's go over this worksheet..."

"Aww—"

"Teacher, tell us something else."

"Yeah, the exam is in two days. Just chat with us, Teacher."

"Teacher, did Chen Guiliang have a girlfriend in high school?"

Faced with the students' enthusiastic requests, Gao Zhan put the worksheet down again. "So, should I keep talking?"

At the home of the cigarette company scion.

Qin Shanshan, who had repeated a year of high school, had just finished the Gaokao again and felt pretty good about it.

She had worked extremely hard for the first half of her repeat year, then slacked off a bit in the second half, but getting into a second-tier university was still a sure thing.

When her mom and dad came home from work, Qin Shanshan was still chatting with her old classmates on QQ.

There was only one computer in the house. Her mom rushed over, "Move, I need to harvest my crops!"

Qin Shanshan rolled her eyes.

She had learned about this stupid game while chatting on QQ, as many of her old classmates were buzzing about it in their group chat.

She had then gotten her parents hooked on it too.

Her dad was a bit better, but her mom was already obsessed, setting alarms in the middle of the night to harvest crops. To steal more crops, her mom had even spread the game at the tobacco company. Now, a whole bunch of employees there were playing *Happy Farm*.

There was even a director who casually recommended the game after a meeting. The very next day, he ordered all his subordinates to add her as a friend!

Qin Shanshan gave up her seat and stood to the side.

Her mom grumbled, "Why is it only the base amount left again? No, I have to steal from all of them!"

Her dad, sitting on the living room sofa watching TV, called towards the study, "Your current condition is called internet addiction."

"What's wrong with taking a moment to harvest my crops?" her mom's mood soured even more.

Her dad said, "You even use SMS to pay for high-level seeds and fertilizer. This game is free to play. How many people do you see paying for it?"

"I didn't use your salary," her mom retorted. "My work subsidizes my phone bill every month. I can't use it all anyway, so it's a waste not to. I just use some of it to top up the game. Besides, after becoming a premium member, I get to keep more of my crops even if they get stolen!"

Her dad didn't know whether to laugh or cry. "Now I get it. I see why Chen Guiliang can be a hundred-millionaire. It's people like you who play his games that prop him up."

Qin Shanshan corrected him, "The one that got venture capital was ByteDance. Although Xiaonei has *Happy Farm*, this game was made by Game Science. My mom plays it on the Game Science platform too."

"It's all the same, they're all his companies," her dad said, his mood lightening. "My boss specifically asked me about it today. Haha, he asked if my daughter was classmates with Chen Guiliang. I said not just classmates, but deskmates. He was very happy to hear that."

"What does your boss have to do with it?" Qin Shanshan asked.

Her dad chuckled, "He can brag about it too. The daughter of his subordinate was deskmates with a hundred-millionaire. Now he'll have something to talk about when he's out drinking."

Qin Shanshan sighed, "Your boss has such low-class tastes!"

In the village.

Her younger maternal uncle was playing cards again, a game with a ten-cent ante.

Someone shouted from outside, "San'er, aren't you going home? A matchmaker's here!"

The uncle, in his thirties and still unmarried due to a slight limp, sprang up as if on springs, tossed his cards, and ran outside.

The uncle ran so fast, he didn't look like he had a limp at all.

Many onlookers had already gathered in the courtyard. A woman in her twenties sat there, looking ill at ease.

The matchmaker pulled the grandparents into the house. "She's 27, from Wadian Township. Her husband died of an illness, and they racked up over 20,000 in medical debt. If you can come up with 30,000 yuan, she's willing to marry him. She's a very capable woman, can do all sorts of farm work, from digging to carrying heavy loads."

"Does she have any children?" Grandpa asked.

The matchmaker said, "A son and a daughter. The son is 6, he's staying with his father's side. The daughter is 3, she can come with her. It's perfect, your Yao San'er is getting on in years. Isn't it great to get a daughter for free?"

Grandma said, "I don't have 30,000 on hand."

"Your grandson has money!"

"I'll have to call and ask."

In the courtyard, the younger uncle and the woman had already taken a liking to each other.
